what_it_shows: Woolworths AU Vegetables sub-aisle: Organic, Prepacked, Capsicum, Tomatoes, Celery, Avocados, Cucumber, Mushrooms, Fresh Herbs/Garlic/Chillies, Zucchini/Eggplant/Squash, Sprouts, Potatoes/Pumpkins, Peas/Beans/Corn/Asparagus; parent aisle splits Fruit, Vegetables, Salad, Prepared Vegetables, Organic, Fresh Herbs/Garlic/Chillies, Snacking
REWE Obst und Gemuese all-categories page: Pilze split into Frische Champignons, Frische Pilze, Getrocknete Pilze

Carrefour.fr rayon: Bio, Fruits, Legumes, Pret a consommer, Jus frais, Fruits et legumes secs, Corbeilles; filters by label (Label Rouge, IGP, AOP, Bio) and origin; Frais et Surgeles is a separate rayon

UNECE FFV standards list: per-produce standards incl. Aubergines, Berry fruits, Ceps, Certain small fruits, Leafy vegetables, Root and tubercle vegetables, Shallots, Strawberries, Truffles, informal citrus variety reference list
UK Specific Marketing Standard (10 produce types; Extra, Class I, Class II) and General Marketing Standard for other fresh fruit, vegetables, nuts, herbs, cultivated mushrooms
USDA AMS voluntary U.S. grade standards per vegetable (asparagus, beets, cabbage, carrots, onions, potatoes, mushrooms, etc.), fresh and processing

Rakuten greengrocer shop: single fruit, single vegetable, boxed fruit by species (strawberry, mikan, grapefruit, persimmon, grape, peach, banana, apple, melon...), sweet potato by named cultivar (Naruto Kintoki, Amakun, Annou)

GS1 GPC: Segment Food/Beverage, Family Fruits Unprepared/Unprocessed (Fresh) with classes Pome Fruits, Kiwifruits, Miscellaneous Fruit and bricks by species (Apples with an Apple Variety attribute, Strawberries, Dates, Durian, Mangos, Lychees); separate families for Vegetables (Non Leaf), Leaf Vegetables, Fresh Cut; Quality (UNECE Standard) attribute
UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection: roughly 1,000 citrus cultivars and relatives, database by alphabet, by category or type, and by fruit-quality data
Orange Pippin variety directory: tree-fruit species (apples, crab-apples, apricots, cherries, peaches, plums, pears) each with named varieties; apples divided dessert, culinary and cider

Capsicum cultivars grouped under five species (annuum, chinense, baccatum, frutescens, pubescens), each with named cultivars (Habanero, Rocoto, De Arbol, Hungarian Wax) and heat in SHU; UK sweet peppers vs chillies, AU/IN capsicum naming
USDA frozen vegetables: U.S. Grade A (90+ points), B (80+), C (70+), Substandard, scored for colour, defects, character, flavour

Specialty Produce encyclopedia (5,600+ articles, grouped by produce family such as apples, mushrooms, greens): Cripps Pink is the varietal name; only about 10% of the crop meets licence and sells under the trademark Pink Lady (first trademarked apple)
MAFF Japan: national standard shipping specifications were abolished in 2002; grading now set by producing regions (prefectures); non-standard (kikakugai) produce sold as own-label lines

Fukushima prefecture standard: fruit and fruit-like vegetables graded Tokushu/Shu/Yu/Ryo, vegetables and mushrooms A/B; size classes by count per box and weight; per-cultivar colour-share tables (Fuji, Tsugaru, Jonagold)
China GB/T 26906-2024 Sweet Cherry: three grades (special, first, second) plus size classes by diameter, soluble solids at least 14 percent; main cultivars named (Hongdeng, Meizao, Summit, Lapins)
USDA AMS fruit grade standards per fruit (apples, apricots, bananas, berries, cherries, citrus, grapes, kiwifruit, mangos, melons, peaches, pears, pineapple, plums); voluntary

Woolworths Fruit and Veg aisle: Fruit, Vegetables, Salad, Prepared Vegetables, Organic, Fresh Herbs/Garlic/Chillies, Snacking; states tomatoes, cucumbers, avocados, capsicums are botanically fruit but filed as vegetables because not sweet; explains by plant part
Woolworths Fruit subcategories: Apples and Pears, Bananas, Berries and Cherries, Citrus, Grapes, Melons and Mangoes, Avocados, Pineapples/Kiwi/Tropical, Asian and Exotic, Cut Fruit
Instacart Fresh Produce: Fresh Fruit, Fresh Vegetables, Fruit and Vegetable Party Trays; Frozen Food is a separate top category

BigBasket Fruits and Vegetables: Fresh Fruits, Fresh Vegetables, Exotic Fruits and Veggies, Herbs and Seasonings, Organic, Cuts and Sprouts; facets for banana varieties (Nendran, Robusta, Yelakki, Poovan) and mango varieties (Alphonso, Kesar, Dasheri, Langra...) as named cultivars
IFPS PLU system: 4-digit (3000/4000 series) or 5-digit codes identify commodity, variety, growing method (prefix 9 for organic) and size; over 1,500 codes; voluntary
PLU list for mushrooms from IFPS: 21 codes by named species or type (button regular small/large, cremini, portabella, shiitake, oyster, enoki, chanterelle, morel, cep, wood ear)
Pepper encyclopedia (215+ profiles) grouping chillies by five Scoville heat tiers: Mild, Medium, Hot, Extra-Hot, Super-Hot, validated against the Chile Pepper Institute
Kroger Frozen Vegetables (171 products) is a Frozen Foods department category with facets such as frozen peas, onions and peppers, pasta and rice mixes

Waitrose Fresh Fruit: Berries, Loose Fruit, Bananas, Apples, Pears, Grapes, Oranges/Lemons/Citrus, Mangos/Melons/Exotic, Peaches and Nectarines, Plums/Apricots, Prepared Fruit, Nuts/Seeds/Dried Fruit, Cherries, Organic, Avocado, Perfectly Ripe
Waitrose Fresh Salad and Herbs is a separate aisle from Fresh Vegetables (cucumber, radish listed here); In Season Fruit and Vegetables is a further aisle
Waitrose Frozen Fruits and Smoothie Mixes (cherries, blueberry, forest fruit mixes) as a frozen-department aisle

Waitrose Frozen Vegetables, Herbs and Rice: Peas, Sweetcorn and Carrots, Beans, Spinach/Broccoli/Cauliflower, Brussels Sprouts, Mixed Vegetables, Parsnips/Celeriac/Squash/Beetroot, Onions, Herbs; frozen chopped garlic, ginger, chilli, coriander
Edible seaweed grouped by colour (green, brown, red) with named types nori, wakame, kombu, dulse, arame, hijiki, sea grapes
NTUC FairPrice Vegetables: Frozen Vegetables, Leafy Vegetables, Mushrooms, Potatoes and Roots, Garlic/Ginger/Onions as sub-groups; kang kong listed; frozen sits inside vegetables

Alliance Bioversity-CIAT guide: vegetables grouped into ten classes by plant part eaten (leafy, root, bulb, stem, flower, fruit, pod, tuber, seed, fungi); notes culinary vegetables that are botanical fruits and overlaps (potato root or tuber, pea pod or legume)

EU marketing standards for fresh produce: Extra, Class I, Class II; ten specific standards (apples, citrus, kiwi, lettuces, peaches/nectarines, pears, strawberries, sweet peppers, table grapes, tomatoes); excluded: potatoes, chilli peppers, sweetcorn, wild mushrooms, sweet potatoes, ripened bananas etc.; general standard for the rest
Waitrose Fresh Vegetables aisle (cherry vine tomatoes, salad onions, large white potatoes listed); sits beside Fresh Fruit, In Season Fruit and Vegetables, and Fresh Salad and Herbs

Orange Pippin apple directory: over 700 named apple and cider varieties, A to Z counts (for example s=94, b=75), each described as dessert, culinary or cider, with synonyms (Albermarle Pippin = Newtown Pippin)

UNECE informal reference list of citrus varieties (2024): grouped lemons, lemon hybrids, Persian limes, West Indian limes, grapefruit, pummelos, oranges (Navel, Red Navel, Valencia, Blood), satsumas, clementines, other mandarins, each with variety, synonyms and trademarks columns
